chunks.content: 96 Some risks aren’t in the P&L—they’re in the fine print. The Sneaky Clause That Can Sink Your Deal Hi Sara, Ever read a contract and thought, “This is so bad it might actually be brilliant”? A while back, I was reviewing a purchase agreement where the seller’s reps and warranties did not survive the closing. As in—once the ink was dry, the buyer had zero legal recourse for anything the seller promised. Nada. Zilch. No take-backs. Here’s the twist: I was representing the seller. And if the buyer’s team wants to skip over indemnification like it’s optional reading? I’m not in the business of saving people from themselves. But if you’re buying a business? You need to know how indemnification works—and why it’s a bigger deal than most people realize. Because not every risk shows up in the P&L. Some of them are buried in the fine print. And they only reveal themselves when something goes sideways. I recorded a video that breaks this all down: — What indemnification really means — When it matters most — And how to avoid the most common buyer-side mistakes Watch the breakdown here. If you’re deep in diligence or negotiating a purchase agreement right now, give it a watch. And if the indemnity language has your eyes crossing? You know where to find me.
